parse_key_values.note: the comment, blank and `[section]` lines are skipped; `export ` is dropped; the spaces around `DB_PORT` are stripped off the key, so it is looked up as 'DB_PORT'; a bare `EMPTY=` gives ''
the line is split on the FIRST `=` only, so every later `=` stays in the value: query strings and base64 padding survive intact
a double-quoted value has \t and friends unescaped (a real tab here), a single-quoted one is literal, and in a bare value a `#` after whitespace starts a comment while `pa#ss` keeps its `#`
lower_keys folds casing, so PORT and port collide into one entry and the later line silently wins — no warning that two keys were merged
a leading UTF-8 BOM (usual in .env files written on Windows) is removed, so the first key is 'DB_HOST' and not '\ufeffDB_HOST'
anything that is not a str is refused up front, not half-parsed
